source.title: Unveiling Latent Knowledge in Chemistry Language Models through Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: J. Cohen; Alexander Hasson; Sara Tanovic

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including supplementary sections, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares individual model neurons with SAE features using chemical-group prediction, descriptor correlations, and interventions. These are different measurements from the claim’s pole audit, and do not test any listed version’s specific measure.
record.gate_note: The paper does not report a fraction of neuron poles with one or more jobs, explanations tested on held-out activating examples, automated simulation scores for neuron explanations, or attribution graphs. It studies a chemistry model’s pooled molecular representations, not Qwen3 or the cited vision-model examples. F1 scores, descriptor associations, prediction results, and ablation results below are the study’s own measurements; cited work and dataset characteristics are omitted.
record.test_reason: This is an SAE study on SMI-TED, a chemistry encoder. It compares SAE features with the 768 dimensions of its pooled molecular embedding, and it adopts the superposition/polysemanticity framing (S1.1) rather than testing it. It does not audit neuron poles or report shares of neurons with one job (V1, V2). It does not study InceptionV1 or pose (V3), compare architectures or tools (V4), build attribution graphs (V5), test explanations on held-out text (V6), or simulate activations to score explanations (V7). Its best-neuron F1, descriptor-count, toxicity and ablation comparisons measure a related but different construct. The 'neurons' are coordinates of a pooled, LayerNorm-projected embedding, not MLP neurons of a language model. The reader's 'tests/T2' contradicts its own judgement that every version is not_tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that SAEs decompose SMI-TED's latent representation into a more interpretable, disentangled basis than raw neurons. They say it spans substructures, physicochemical descriptors and functional concepts, and isolates the toxicity signal more compactly. They also claim causally relevant steering 'not afforded by' the entangled neuron basis. They acknowledge limits: unscaled manual interpretation, a single architecture, open out-of-distribution generalisation, and the need for stronger baselines.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains TopK SAEs on SMI-TED’s pooled molecular representations and evaluates chemical concepts and molecular decoding. It does not use the original neuron-pole audit method or evaluate Qwen3 neuron-job shares.
record.method_sensitivity: The SAE configuration is selected from a grid search; the paper reports reconstruction fidelity varies with sparsity and expansion factor. The primary feature analysis uses 8× expansion and k = 80.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 14 functional groups, the best single embedding dimension detects the group far worse than the best SAE feature for rare motifs. Examples: nitrate 0.056 vs 1.000; cyanamide 0.030 vs 0.667. Common motifs score nearly equal: alkyl carbon 0.938 vs 0.945; carbonyl 0.735 vs 0.745.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a chemistry encoder's pooled embedding, individual dimensions detect common substructures about as well as SAE features but rarely detect rare ones. Single units appear not to be dedicated to low-prevalence concepts.

fits_no_version.finding: Each Mordred descriptor correlates (|ρ|≥0.3) with about 66 raw dimensions vs about 6 SAE features. Mean pairwise correlation is 0.162 for raw dimensions vs 0.016 for SAE features. The top 100 relationships map to 69 dimensions, 100 SAE features, 3 PCA components and 5 NMF factors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In SMI-TED's pooled embedding, descriptor information is spread across many correlated dimensions, and SAE features give a sparser, less correlated basis.

fits_no_version.finding: MITOTOX toxicity AUCpr is equal for both bases: 0.603 from raw dimensions, 0.606 from SAE features (p=0.75). There are 213 significant raw-dimension predictors vs 19 significant SAE features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The SAE basis is information-preserving and more compact than raw dimensions for toxicity prediction.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean-ablating single dimensions never produced a valid changed molecule (14/768 gave invalid strings). Zero-ablating 749 of 2,501 active SAE features produced valid changed molecules, with illustrative substructure swaps. The two intervention protocols differ.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single SAE features in SMI-TED can steer decoded structures, whereas single embedding dimensions are not individually critical.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says materials needed to reproduce results, including model weights, will be made available at publication.
record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2025 Workshop: AI for Accelerated Materials Design
record.problems: Only one model architecture is analysed. The authors state that feature interpretation is not scaled, generalisation to out-of-distribution molecules is open, and more robust baselines are needed. The study’s chemical prediction and reconstruction metrics do not directly establish human-readable neuron-job shares or circuit-level sufficiency.
record.rows_left_out: None. Included the reported Table S3 substructure results, Section 3.2 and 3.3 comparisons, and the quantitative and qualitative ablation outcomes relevant to neuron-versus-feature analysis.

untested.parts: All: no pole audit or job shares; uses SMI-TED, not Qwen3-32B.
All: no neuron-job shares in any language model, dense or MoE, or across scale.
All: no InceptionV1 or canonical polysemantic neuron re-analysis.
All: no comparison of interpretable-neuron share across architectures, regularization or tool quality.
All: no attribution graphs or replacement-model comparison.
All: no test of activating-example explanations predicting firing.
All: no simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The study implicitly sits opposite the essay's thesis by assuming superposition, but it does not measure anything the versions name. Its 'neurons' are pooled-embedding coordinates after a linear projection, a basis with no obvious privilege, so a weak per-unit result says little about MLP-neuron cleanliness in LLMs. The neuron-vs-feature ablation comparison uses different intervention protocols (mean vs zero, different molecule selection).

versions.untested_parts: Does not audit neuron poles or report the shares with one job, two related jobs, or not-yet-understood jobs; uses SMI-TED rather than Qwen3-32B.
Uses one chemistry model and does not measure the claimed shares across models, architectures, or scales.
Does not study InceptionV1, cat-and-car examples, pose, or recursive generalization.
Does not estimate interpretability shares across vision architectures or tool quality.
Does not build attribution graphs or compare neuron-based explanations with a replacement model and reconstruction error.
Does not test whether explanations written from activating examples predict firing on separate examples.
Does not score natural-language neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text; its chemical-group F1 evaluation is a different measure.

rows.measure: Neurons producing invalid SMILES after ablation
rows.note: The study states no neuron interventions produced a valid but different molecule.
rows.check: Neuron ablation sets the value to the distribution mean on its top and bottom 100 molecules. SAE ablation (r43) instead zeroes the feature on molecules where it is active. The interventions differ, so r41/r42 vs r43 is not a like-for-like comparison of steerability.
